reviews.author: INcLine Museum_IncLine
reviews.text:
A casual wine bar that wine lovers must visit!

Tap Shop Bar Hapjeong is a large wine and dining bar located on the first floor of H Square, 81 Yanghwa-ro, a 5-minute walk from Hapjeong Station. As its 5th branch in Seoul, its spacious and sophisticated interior is impressive. Like a pub, you can freely choose wine and food from the menu and pay by card and member recharge system.

Hundreds of types of whiskey and wine are on display and can be ordered by the bottle or glass, so anyone can find the style they want. The wine prices are not much cheaper than those at online and offline aging stores, but they are reasonable in that you can drink them right at the bar. A variety of snacks are available in the 10,000 to 20,000 won range, including seasonal oysters (14,900), tteokbokki (9,900), kimchi fried rice (10,900), and black bean ramen (11,900), as well as cheese, snacks, olives, and simple finger foods.

Champagne set and snack + wine promotions are held regularly, so it's worth looking for event menu discounts every time you visit. Thanks to the spacious tables and rooms, it is suitable for gatherings and group visits, and maintains a noisy yet casual and clean atmosphere.

The staff helps with wine selection, making it easy for beginners to visit. Although it is a bit disappointing that there are no whiskey glasses, it is a popular wine bar in the Hapjeong and Hongdae areas. After actually visiting, the pros are the fun of choosing and drinking hundreds of wines, reasonable prices, spacious space, and a clean atmosphere. The cons are that rechargeable payment is a bit cumbersome, and some of the wine scents and atmosphere are disappointing.

reviews.author: Majimata
reviews.text:
Gyeongui Line Forest Park is an urban park about 6 km long connecting Mapo-gu and Yongsan-gu, Seoul, and is a space created by reorganizing the site of the discontinued Gyeongui Line railway.

Traces of the old railroad track remain here and there, and it is divided into sections, with small streams, fountains, walking trails, and bicycle paths stretching out between well-manicured bushes, making it more suitable for a small forest path in the city than a park.
As it crosses Hongik University Station, which is crowded with tourists, there are many pretty cafes and restaurants nearby, making it a good date course, and there are benches here and there, making it a good place to take a leisurely rest.
(The cute-looking Mapo Circular Train bus stop, which goes to important locations in Mapo, is located near the GoMango store, so take it if you are interested.)

The buildings next to Red Road Power Plant beyond Hongik University Station seem to be in need of improvement as they are enclosed structures that make it difficult to look inside.

It's a bit small in size to recommend, but it has a romantic atmosphere and is great for taking pictures, so it's not a bad healing course.
